/-!
# Conjecture 2.22

by Sh. S. Kemkhadze

a) An abstract group-theoretic property $\Sigma$ is said to be *radical (in our sense)* if,
in any group $G$, the subgroup $\Sigma(G)$ generated by all normal $\Sigma$-subgroups is a
$\Sigma$-subgroup itself (called the *$\Sigma$-radical* of $G$). A radical property $\Sigma$
is said to be *strongly radical* if, for any group $G$, the factor-group $G/\Sigma(G)$
contains no non-trivial normal $\Sigma$-subgroups. Is the property $\overline{RN}$ radical?
strongly radical?

Here $\overline{RN}$ is Kurosh's class of generalized solvable groups. A *normal system* of a
group $G$ is a set of subgroups of $G$ that contains the trivial subgroup and $G$, is linearly
ordered by inclusion, is complete (closed under unions and intersections of arbitrary
subfamilies), and in which $A$ is a normal subgroup of $B$ for every jump $(A, B)$ (a pair of
members $A < B$ with no member strictly between them). The quotients $B/A$ over the jumps are
the *factors* of the system, and the system is *solvable* if all its factors are abelian.
A group is an $\overline{RN}$-group if every one of its normal systems can be refined to a
solvable normal system, where a refinement of a system is a system containing it.
(In Robinson's terminology, a normal system is a *series*.)

*References:*
- [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46), Problem 2.22
- A. G. Kurosh, *The Theory of Groups*, Vol. II
- D. J. S. Robinson, *Finiteness Conditions and Generalized Soluble Groups*, Part 1
-/

def IsJump (S : Set (Subgroup G)) (A B : Subgroup G) : Prop :=
  A ∈ S ∧ B ∈ S ∧ A < B ∧ ∀ C ∈ S, ¬ (A < C ∧ C < B)
blocks.docstring:
`(A, B)` is a *jump* of a set `S` of subgroups of `G`: `A` and `B` are members of `S` with
`A < B`, and no member of `S` lies strictly between them.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Mathlib's `CovBy` (`⋖`) works in the ambient lattice, not relative to the set S; using it on the subtype `↥S` was possible but less readable.
justification.name: Kourovka.«2.22».IsJump
justification.why_needed: Expresses that (A, B) is a jump of a set S of subgroups (A, B ∈ S, A < B, no member of S strictly between), needed to talk about the factors of a normal system of arbitrary (possibly non-well-ordered) order type.

blocks.name: IsJump
blocks.text:
/-- `(A, B)` is a *jump* of a set `S` of subgroups of `G`: `A` and `B` are members of `S` with
`A < B`, and no member of `S` lies strictly between them. -/
def IsJump (S : Set (Subgroup G)) (A B : Subgroup G) : Prop :=
  A ∈ S ∧ B ∈ S ∧ A < B ∧ ∀ C ∈ S, ¬ (A < C ∧ C < B)

structure IsNormalSystem (S : Set (Subgroup G)) : Prop where
  bot_mem : ⊥ ∈ S
  top_mem : ⊤ ∈ S
  isChain : IsChain (· ≤ ·) S
  sSup_mem : ∀ T ⊆ S, sSup T ∈ S
  sInf_mem : ∀ T ⊆ S, sInf T ∈ S

blocks.docstring:
A *normal system* of `G` (Kurosh; a *series* in Robinson's terminology): a set `S` of
subgroups of `G` that contains `⊥` and `⊤`, is linearly ordered by inclusion, is complete
(closed under joins and meets of arbitrary subfamilies; for a chain of subgroups the join is the
union), and in which `A` is a normal subgroup of `B` for every jump `(A, B)`. The quotients
`B ⧸ A` over the jumps are the *factors* of `S`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Mathlib `CompositionSeries` (finite length only, and requires maximality), `IsSolvable`/`derivedSeries` (finite derived series only), `IsChain`.
justification.name: Kourovka.«2.22».IsNormalSystem
justification.why_needed: Kurosh's normal system (Robinson's 'series'): a set of subgroups containing ⊥ and ⊤, linearly ordered by inclusion, complete (closed under sSup and sInf of arbitrary subfamilies), with A normal in B at every jump. Mathlib has no notion of (transfinite) series/normal system.

blocks.code:
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem isNormalSystem_pair : IsNormalSystem ({⊥, ⊤} : Set (Subgroup G)) where
  bot_mem := by simp
  top_mem := by simp
  isChain := by
    rintro A (rfl | rfl) B (rfl | rfl) _ <;> simp
  sSup_mem T hT := by
    by_cases h : ⊤ ∈ T
    · simp [top_le_iff.mp (le_sSup h)]
    · have : sSup T = ⊥ := le_bot_iff.mp <| sSup_le fun K hK => by
        rcases hT hK with rfl | rfl
        · exact le_rfl
        · exact absurd hK h
      simp [this]
  sInf_mem T hT := by
    by_cases h : ⊥ ∈ T
    · simp [le_bot_iff.mp (sInf_le h)]
    · have : sInf T = ⊤ := top_le_iff.mp <| le_sInf fun K hK => by
        rcases hT hK with rfl | rfl
        · exact absurd hK h
        · exact le_rfl
      simp [this]
  normal_of_isJump A B h := by
    obtain ⟨hA, -, hlt, -⟩ := h
    rcases hA with rfl | rfl
    · rw [Subgroup.bot_subgroupOf]; infer_instance
    · exact absurd hlt not_top_lt
blocks.docstring: The trivial system `{⊥, ⊤}` is a normal system of every group.

def IsSolvableNormalSystem (S : Set (Subgroup G)) : Prop :=
  IsNormalSystem S ∧ ∀ A B, IsJump S A B → ⁅B, B⁆ ≤ A
blocks.docstring:
A normal system `S` of `G` is *solvable* if all its factors are abelian, i.e. `⁅B, B⁆ ≤ A`
for every jump `(A, B)` of `S`.

justification.name: Kourovka.«2.22».IsSolvableNormalSystem
justification.why_needed: A normal system all of whose factors B/A over jumps are abelian, expressed as ⁅B, B⁆ ≤ A.

blocks.name: IsSolvableNormalSystem
blocks.text:
/-- A normal system `S` of `G` is *solvable* if all its factors are abelian, i.e. `⁅B, B⁆ ≤ A`
for every jump `(A, B)` of `S`. -/
def IsSolvableNormalSystem (S : Set (Subgroup G)) : Prop :=
  IsNormalSystem S ∧ ∀ A B, IsJump S A B → ⁅B, B⁆ ≤ A

def IsRNBarGroup (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ S : Set (Subgroup G), IsNormalSystem S → ∃ T, S ⊆ T ∧ IsSolvableNormalSystem T
blocks.docstring:
A group `G` is an $\overline{RN}$-group (Kurosh) if every normal system of `G` can be
refined to a solvable normal system of `G`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: `IsSolvable` (only captures finite solvable groups; RN̄ is a much wider generalized-solvable class).
justification.name: Kourovka.«2.22».IsRNBarGroup
justification.why_needed: Kurosh's class RN̄: every normal system of G can be refined to (is contained in) a solvable normal system of G. Not in Mathlib or the repo.

blocks.name: IsRNBarGroup
blocks.text:
/-- A group `G` is an $\overline{RN}$-group (Kurosh) if every normal system of `G` can be
refined to a solvable normal system of `G`. -/
def IsRNBarGroup (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ S : Set (Subgroup G), IsNormalSystem S → ∃ T, S ⊆ T ∧ IsSolvableNormalSystem T

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsRNBarGroup.of_isMulCommutative [IsMulCommutative G] : IsRNBarGroup G := by
  intro S hS
  refine ⟨S, le_rfl, hS, fun A B _ => ?_⟩
  rw [Subgroup.commutator_le]
  intro g₁ _ g₂ _
  simp [commutatorElement_def]
blocks.docstring:
Every abelian group is an $\overline{RN}$-group: each of its normal systems is already
solvable.

blocks.code:
def rnBarRadical (G : Type*) [Group G] : Subgroup G :=
  sSup {N : Subgroup G | N.Normal ∧ IsRNBarGroup N}
blocks.docstring:
The $\overline{RN}$-radical `Σ(G)` of `G`: the subgroup generated by all normal
$\overline{RN}$-subgroups of `G`. Since the trivial subgroup is a normal
$\overline{RN}$-subgroup, this join is never over an empty family.

justification.closest_existing_considered: No radical-of-a-class construction exists in Mathlib (only e.g. `Subgroup.center`, `Subgroup.fittingSubgroup`-style specific subgroups are absent as well).
justification.name: Kourovka.«2.22».rnBarRadical
justification.why_needed: The Σ-radical Σ(G) of the statement for Σ = RN̄: the subgroup generated (sSup) by all normal RN̄-subgroups of G. Proved normal in `rnBarRadical_normal` so the factor group G ⧸ Σ(G) can be formed.

theorem le_rnBarRadical {N : Subgroup G} (hN : N.Normal) (h : IsRNBarGroup N) :
    N ≤ rnBarRadical G :=
  le_sSup ⟨hN, h⟩
blocks.docstring: Every normal $\overline{RN}$-subgroup of `G` is contained in the $\overline{RN}$-radical.

blocks.code:
instance rnBarRadical_normal : (rnBarRadical G).Normal where
  conj_mem n hn g := by
    have h : rnBarRadical G ≤ (rnBarRadical G).comap (MulAut.conj g).toMonoidHom :=
      sSup_le fun N hN x hx =>
        Subgroup.mem_comap.mpr (Subgroup.mem_sSup_of_mem hN (hN.1.conj_mem x hx g))
    simpa using h hn
blocks.docstring: The $\overline{RN}$-radical is a normal subgroup, being generated by normal subgroups.

justification.name: Kourovka.«2.22».normal_sSup (theorem) and instance rnBarRadical_normal
justification.why_needed: Mathlib only has `Subgroup.sup_normal` for binary joins; normality of `sSup` of a set of normal subgroups is needed to form the quotient `G ⧸ rnBarRadical G`. Proved (not sorried) in the file. This is reusable mathematics that would ideally live in FormalConjecturesForMathlib, but the task restricted output to a single file.

  conj_mem n hn g := by
    have h : rnBarRadical G ≤ (rnBarRadical G).comap (MulAut.conj g).toMonoidHom :=
      sSup_le fun N hN x hx =>
        Subgroup.mem_comap.mpr (Subgroup.mem_sSup_of_mem hN (hN.1.conj_mem x hx g))
    simpa using h hn

claims.decomposer_note: Yes/no Prop over all groups G (quantify `G : Type` after `answer(sorry) ↔`): the join Σ(G) of all normal $\overline{RN}$-subgroups of G is itself an $\overline{RN}$-group; here $\overline{RN}$ is Kurosh's class of groups in which every normal system (complete chain of subgroups, each normal in its successor) can be refined to a solvable normal system (all factors abelian), equivalently every serial section B/A is an RN-group — this class is not in Mathlib and must be defined, and the trivial subgroup is always an $\overline{RN}$-subgroup so Σ(G) is well defined (never an empty join issue).
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates state this slot with the same shape `answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], IsRNBarGroup (rnBarRadical G)` and mathematically equivalent bespoke definitions (Kurosh normal system = complete chain of subgroups closed under sSup/sInf of arbitrary subfamilies, hence containing ⊥ and ⊤, with A ◁ B at every jump; solvable = ⁅B,B⁆ ≤ A at jumps; RN̄ = every normal system is contained in a solvable normal system). c05 was chosen as the base because its radical is the literal `sSup` of the set of normal RN̄-subgroups (c01/c06/c08 use a normalClosure detour, c06 uses heavyweight bundled structures), its definitions are readable `structure`/`def`s with docstrings, and it includes proved API/test lemmas for the bespoke definitions as CONTRIBUTING.md asks. Edits: normality proof folded into a named instance, abelian lemma generalized to `IsMulCommutative`, added the `⊥`-is-RN̄ test (from c07) documenting the non-empty join, docstring tightened (refinement defined explicitly).

claims.decomposer_note: By the statement's definition 'strongly radical' presupposes 'radical', so the Prop is the conjunction (∀ G, Σ(G) is an $\overline{RN}$-group) ∧ (∀ G, every normal $\overline{RN}$-subgroup of G/Σ(G) is trivial), where Σ(G) = join of all normal $\overline{RN}$-subgroups (normal, so the quotient exists); this is a strictly stronger form of the first question of part a), hence a variant rather than a co-equal part.
claims.reviewer_why: Stated as the conjunction (∀ G, IsRNBarGroup (rnBarRadical G)) ∧ (∀ G, ∀ N : Subgroup (G ⧸ rnBarRadical G), N.Normal → IsRNBarGroup N → N = ⊥), exactly as the decomposition table prescribes (strongly radical presupposes radical). The quotient is well-formed via the proved `Normal` instance on the sSup of normal subgroups. All candidates agree on this shape; c05's version is used for consistency with the chosen definitions.

decomposition_objections.text: None. The table's primary description of RN̄ (every normal system refines to a solvable normal system) is the one formalized; its parenthetical 'equivalently every serial section B/A is an RN-group' was not relied upon.

/-!
# Conjecture 2.22

by Sh. S. Kemkhadze

group $G$ is a set of subgroups of $G$ that contains the trivial subgroup and $G$, is linearly
ordered by inclusion, is complete (closed under unions and intersections of arbitrary

- [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46), Problem 2.22

namespace Kourovka.«2.22»

variable {G : Type*} [Group G]

/-- `(A, B)` is a *jump* of a set `S` of subgroups of `G`: `A` and `B` are members of `S` with
`A < B`, and no member of `S` lies strictly between them. -/
def IsJump (S : Set (Subgroup G)) (A B : Subgroup G) : Prop :=
  A ∈ S ∧ B ∈ S ∧ A < B ∧ ∀ C ∈ S, ¬ (A < C ∧ C < B)

/-- A *normal system* of `G` (Kurosh; a *series* in Robinson's terminology): a set `S` of
subgroups of `G` that contains `⊥` and `⊤`, is linearly ordered by inclusion, is complete
(closed under joins and meets of arbitrary subfamilies; for a chain of subgroups the join is the
union), and in which `A` is a normal subgroup of `B` for every jump `(A, B)`. The quotients
`B ⧸ A` over the jumps are the *factors* of `S`. -/
structure IsNormalSystem (S : Set (Subgroup G)) : Prop where
  bot_mem : ⊥ ∈ S
  top_mem : ⊤ ∈ S
  isChain : IsChain (· ≤ ·) S
  sSup_mem : ∀ T ⊆ S, sSup T ∈ S
  sInf_mem : ∀ T ⊆ S, sInf T ∈ S
  normal_of_isJump : ∀ A B, IsJump S A B → (A.subgroupOf B).Normal

/-- The trivial system `{⊥, ⊤}` is a normal system of every group. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem isNormalSystem_pair : IsNormalSystem ({⊥, ⊤} : Set (Subgroup G)) where
  bot_mem := by simp
  top_mem := by simp
  isChain := by
    rintro A (rfl | rfl) B (rfl | rfl) _ <;> simp
  sSup_mem T hT := by
    by_cases h : ⊤ ∈ T
    · simp [top_le_iff.mp (le_sSup h)]
    · have : sSup T = ⊥ := le_bot_iff.mp <| sSup_le fun K hK => by
        rcases hT hK with rfl | rfl
        · exact le_rfl
        · exact absurd hK h
      simp [this]
  sInf_mem T hT := by
    by_cases h : ⊥ ∈ T
    · simp [le_bot_iff.mp (sInf_le h)]
    · have : sInf T = ⊤ := top_le_iff.mp <| le_sInf fun K hK => by
        rcases hT hK with rfl | rfl
        · exact absurd hK h
        · exact le_rfl
      simp [this]
  normal_of_isJump A B h := by
    obtain ⟨hA, -, hlt, -⟩ := h
    rcases hA with rfl | rfl
    · rw [Subgroup.bot_subgroupOf]; infer_instance
    · exact absurd hlt not_top_lt

/-- A normal system `S` of `G` is *solvable* if all its factors are abelian, i.e. `⁅B, B⁆ ≤ A`
for every jump `(A, B)` of `S`. -/
def IsSolvableNormalSystem (S : Set (Subgroup G)) : Prop :=
  IsNormalSystem S ∧ ∀ A B, IsJump S A B → ⁅B, B⁆ ≤ A

/-- A group `G` is an $\overline{RN}$-group (Kurosh) if every normal system of `G` can be
refined to a solvable normal system of `G`. -/
def IsRNBarGroup (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ S : Set (Subgroup G), IsNormalSystem S → ∃ T, S ⊆ T ∧ IsSolvableNormalSystem T

/-- Every abelian group is an $\overline{RN}$-group: each of its normal systems is already
solvable. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsRNBarGroup.of_isMulCommutative [IsMulCommutative G] : IsRNBarGroup G := by
  intro S hS
  refine ⟨S, le_rfl, hS, fun A B _ => ?_⟩
  rw [Subgroup.commutator_le]
  intro g₁ _ g₂ _
  simp [commutatorElement_def]

/-- The trivial subgroup is a normal $\overline{RN}$-subgroup of every group. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isRNBarGroup_bot : IsRNBarGroup (⊥ : Subgroup G) :=
  IsRNBarGroup.of_isMulCommutative

/-- The $\overline{RN}$-radical `Σ(G)` of `G`: the subgroup generated by all normal
$\overline{RN}$-subgroups of `G`. Since the trivial subgroup is a normal
$\overline{RN}$-subgroup, this join is never over an empty family. -/
def rnBarRadical (G : Type*) [Group G] : Subgroup G :=
  sSup {N : Subgroup G | N.Normal ∧ IsRNBarGroup N}

/-- Every normal $\overline{RN}$-subgroup of `G` is contained in the $\overline{RN}$-radical. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem le_rnBarRadical {N : Subgroup G} (hN : N.Normal) (h : IsRNBarGroup N) :
    N ≤ rnBarRadical G :=
  le_sSup ⟨hN, h⟩

/-- The $\overline{RN}$-radical is a normal subgroup, being generated by normal subgroups. -/
instance rnBarRadical_normal : (rnBarRadical G).Normal where
  conj_mem n hn g := by
    have h : rnBarRadical G ≤ (rnBarRadical G).comap (MulAut.conj g).toMonoidHom :=
      sSup_le fun N hN x hx =>
        Subgroup.mem_comap.mpr (Subgroup.mem_sSup_of_mem hN (hN.1.conj_mem x hx g))
    simpa using h hn

/-- The $\overline{RN}$-radical of an abelian group is the whole group. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem rnBarRadical_eq_top [IsMulCommutative G] : rnBarRadical G = ⊤ :=
  top_le_iff.mp <| le_rnBarRadical inferInstance IsRNBarGroup.of_isMulCommutative

/--
Is the property $\overline{RN}$ radical? That is, for every group $G$, is the subgroup
$\Sigma(G)$ generated by all normal $\overline{RN}$-subgroups of $G$ itself an
$\overline{RN}$-group?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«2.22».parts.a : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], IsRNBarGroup (rnBarRadical G) := by
  sorry

/--
Is the property $\overline{RN}$ strongly radical? That is, is $\overline{RN}$ radical
(for every group $G$, the subgroup $\Sigma(G)$ generated by all normal
$\overline{RN}$-subgroups of $G$ is an $\overline{RN}$-group), and moreover, for every group
$G$, does the factor-group $G/\Sigma(G)$ contain no non-trivial normal
$\overline{RN}$-subgroups?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«2.22».parts.a.variants.strongly_radical : answer(sorry) ↔
    (∀ (G : Type) [Group G], IsRNBarGroup (rnBarRadical G)) ∧
      ∀ (G : Type) [Group G] (N : Subgroup (G ⧸ rnBarRadical G)),
        N.Normal → IsRNBarGroup N → N = ⊥ := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«2.22»

items: RN̄ is formalized by Kurosh's direct definition (every normal system has a solvable normal-system refinement, i.e. S ⊆ T with T solvable), not by the 'every serial section is RN' reformulation mentioned in the table notes.

A normal system is required to be complete (closed under sSup and sInf of all subfamilies T ⊆ S); since members form a chain, sSup T is the set-theoretic union, so this is exactly Kurosh's/Robinson's completeness. ⊥ ∈ S and ⊤ ∈ S are listed explicitly although they follow from completeness (sSup ∅ = ⊥, sInf ∅ = ⊤).
Normality at a jump is expressed as `(A.subgroupOf B).Normal`; abelian factor B/A is expressed as `⁅B, B⁆ ≤ A` (equivalent for A ≤ B, and it also implies A ⊴ B).
Groups are quantified over `G : Type` (universe 0), following the existing Kourovka files (e.g. 1_40.lean).
The 'strongly radical' slot is the conjunction of the radical property and the quotient condition, as the decomposition table prescribes; `answer(True)` means 'yes'.

Two short API lemmas and one test are included with proofs (`isNormalSystem_pair`, `IsRNBarGroup.of_commGroup`, `rnBarRadical_normal`, `rnBarRadical_eq_top_of_commGroup`) to check that the bespoke definitions are non-vacuous.

reviewer_notes: The problem's only non-standard ingredient is Kurosh's class RN̄, absent from Mathlib; it is defined in the file following Kurosh–Chernikov ('every normal system can be refined to a solvable normal system'). Modeling checks: (1) completeness (closure under sSup/sInf of all subfamilies, incl. the empty one) is essential and included — without it a dense chain or a non-terminating ascending chain would make 'solvable normal system' vacuous; for a chain of subgroups sSup is the set-theoretic union, so this matches Kurosh's 'unions and intersections'. (2) Normality at jumps is `(A.subgroupOf B).Normal`, abelian factor is `⁅B, B⁆ ≤ A`, both correct given A < B. (3) A 'Σ-subgroup' is a subgroup that is RN̄ as an abstract group (`IsRNBarGroup ↥N`), so the property is isomorphism-invariant as required by 'abstract group-theoretic property'. (4) Σ(G) is `sSup {N | N.Normal ∧ IsRNBarGroup N}`; ⊥ is always in the set (proved as a test), so no empty-join issue. (5) `answer(True)` = 'yes, RN̄ is (strongly) radical'; groups quantified as `G : Type` after `answer(sorry) ↔`, matching the existing Kourovka files. No candidate omitted a slot and no candidate raised objections to the decomposition; I found none either. Residual uncertainty is only about the literature definition of RN̄ being exactly 'every normal system refines to a solvable one' (I could not consult Kurosh's text offline, but the slot notes and all candidates agree, and the equivalent 'every factor of every normal system is RN' formulation mentioned in the notes was deliberately not used). Final file compiled with `lake env lean` (only 'declaration uses sorry' warnings) and with `lake --wfail build` when placed at FormalConjectures/Kourovka/2_22.lean.
statement:
a) An abstract group-theoretic property $\Sigma$ is said to be radical $($in our sense) if, in any group $G$, the subgroup $\Sigma(G)$ generated by all normal $\Sigma
$-subgroups is a $\Sigma $-subgroup itself (called the $\Sigma $-radical of $G$). A radical property $\Sigma$ is said to be strongly radical if, for any group $G$, the factor-group $G/\Sigma(G)$ contains no non-trivial normal $\Sigma
$-subgroups. Is the property $\,\overline{\! RN}$ radical? strongly radical?
